content:
Topology can feel abstract at first because it studies properties of spaces that don’t change under continuous stretching or bending—no tearing or gluing. Before jumping into chain complexes and homology, it helps to think about the simplest idea: what does it mean for two shapes to be “the same” in topology?

Imagine a coffee cup and a donut (torus). Topologically, they are the same because you can deform one into the other without cutting or attaching new parts. This notion of equivalence is the foundation of topology.

Does this idea of “continuous deformation” as a notion of sameness feel clear? If so, we can move next to how algebraic tools like chain complexes capture these shape properties.
